message.reasoning:
I need to write JUnit 4 tests for jsoup's Element class, aiming for maximum branch coverage. Since this is Defects4J Jsoup-87b, the jsoup source itself should already be compiled into the project's classpath. So other classes in org.jsoup package like Document, Tag, Attributes, TextNode, DataNode, Comment, CDataNode, Elements, and NodeUtils should be fair game to import and use, since they're part of the same codebase compiled alongside Element. The restriction to "JUnit 4 and libraries in classpath" must refer to external dependencies, not the jsoup source itself which naturally gets compiled in. I'm wondering though if NodeUtils actually exists and whether methods calling NodeUtils.parser(this) would work without an attached parser. I'll focus tests on areas that don't depend heavily on NodeUtils for safety, while still covering key branches - like testing constructor null handling through Validate.notNull exceptions for tag and baseUri parameters, and examining ensureChildNodes behavior. I'll also test hasAttributes and attributes() when null (requiring the Element(Tag, String) constructor), childNodeSize with and without children, nodeName/tagName, and cautiously check tagName(String) which calls NodeUtils.parser. Then I plan to cover tag(), isBlock() comparing block vs inline tags, id() with and without the attribute set, attr(String,String) chaining, and attr(String,boolean) branches. For dataset() I'll just call it without deep checks. For parent() I need tests with null and with an actual parent set. For parents() I should test accumulateParents walking multiple levels and stopping at a "#root" tagged element, constructing a fake root Element to verify parents() excludes it. Then I want child(int) tests for valid and out-of-bounds indices, children() tests mixing TextNode and Element to confirm only Elements are returned, and a test for childElementsList caching -- appending a child, calling children(), appending another, and confirming the list updates rather than staying stale. I also need coverage for textNodes() and dataNodes() with a DataNode added, select(String) and selectFirst using Selector with a simple tag selector, is(String) and is(Evaluator), appendChild with null throwing Validate.notNull and normal appends checking childNodeSize and siblingIndex, appendTo(Element), prependChild with null and normal cases, and insertChildren(int, Collection) and its varargs counterpart testing negative index wraparound, out-of-bounds exceptions, and valid inserts. Then I need tests for null children collections throwing exceptions, appendElement/prependElement using NodeUtils.parser, appendText/prependText with null-throws and normal cases, append/prepend(String html) via parseFragmentInput, before/after delegating to Node superclass methods, empty() clearing children, wrap(String) delegating to super, and cssSelector() covering id-based selectors, class-based selectors without id, root-level elements without a parent, and elements with a parent context. For the parent case I'll design a nested scenario: a standalone element with no parent returns just its tag/class selector directly, while a child under a non-Document parent triggers the " > " prefix and possibly ":nth-child" disambiguation when sibling elements share the same tag and no distinguishing class/id -- I'll set up a div with two identical span children to test that select() finds duplicates and adds the nth-child qualifier. Next I'm planning tests for sibling-related methods: siblingElements() with a null parent returning empty, nextElementSibling() returning null at the boundary, nextElementSiblings() relying on the Elements.nextAll() implementation, previousElementSibling()/previousElementSiblings() with similar boundary checks, and firstElementSibling() which has a potential off-by-one bug where a lone element might incorrectly return null since the size check requires more than one sibling -- a good candidate for fault detection. I'm also noting elementSiblingIndex() needs a null-parent case returning zero. I'm continuing through lastElementSibling() with the same bug pattern, then moving to the getElementsBy* family -- getElementsByTag, getElementById, getElementsByClass, and various attribute-based selectors -- each needing validation tests for empty/blank input via notEmpty checks, plus normal search-hit and search-miss cases. I'm also planning tests for getElementsByAttributeValueMatching with both a Pattern and a String regex, including a case with an invalid regex to confirm PatternSyntaxException gets wrapped into an IllegalArgumentException. Beyond that, I'm mapping out tests for index-based filters, text-containing filters, text/wholeText/ownText extraction (including nested elements, block-tag spacing, and br handling), preserveWhitespace behavior on pre tags, hasText(), data() across DataNode/Comment/CDataNode combinations, and className()/classNames() trimming and default behavior. I'm also planning hasClass() coverage across its many branches—no class attribute, shorter/equal/mismatched lengths, substring vs whole-word matches, trailing class at string end, and whitespace toggling between classes—plus addClass/removeClass/toggleClass scenarios and val()/val(String) behavior differing for textarea versus other tags. For outerHtmlHead/outerHtmlTail and other package-private methods, I'm considering placing ElementTest in org.jsoup.nodes so it can directly access and test those members, which is a common white-box testing approach. Continuing through the remaining methods: html(Appendable) with a StringBuilder, html(String) for clearing and setting content, clone() verifying structural copies with independent modifications, shallowClone() confirming no children are copied, and doClone(Node) tested indirectly through clone(). Given the sheer number of methods, I'll prioritize covering as many branches as reasonably achievable. Some methods like tagName(String), appendElement, append(String), and html(String) rely on internal parser logic I don't have full visibility into, so I'll write these tests cautiously -- confirming they don't throw unexpected exceptions rather than asserting exact internal behavior I can't verify. I'll proceed with reasonable confidence and write a comprehensive test class organized by method groups, covering boundary, null, and empty cases, with the necessary imports for jsoup nodes, selectors, and JUnit. I should also verify how Validate.notNull behaves, likely throwing an IllegalArgumentException. I'll write tests expecting IllegalArgumentException for these violations, and also consider edge cases like firstElementSibling/lastElementSibling returning null when there's only one sibling—this matches the source's explicit logic rather than being a guessed behavior, so I'll test for that documented null case accordingly. I also want to test Element construction: checking that hasAttributes() is false before lazy initialization, verifying tagName() behavior with the default Tag.valueOf settings using lowercase input to avoid case-sensitivity issues, and confirming that a null tag argument triggers Validate.notNull. The null-tag scenario for the simpler String constructor is riskier since Tag.valueOf's internal null handling isn't visible, so I'll focus explicit null-check tests on the Element(Tag, String, Attributes) constructor instead, where Validate.notNull calls are clearly present. Now drafting the full test file, accessing package-private members like childNodes directly since the test will live in the same org.jsoup.nodes package. Protected methods like doSetBaseUri, ensureChildNodes, and nodelistChanged are also reachable this way since protected access extends to same-package callers in Java. For outerHtmlHead and outerHtmlTail I'll need a Document.OutputSettings instance, which should have a public no-arg constructor I can use. Now I want to focus test coverage on the actual branching logic inside Element.java itself, not inside helper classes like Validate - since those internal checks aren't part of Element's own conditional paths I don't need to exercise both sides of them separately, just call the methods normally and trust they delegate correctly. Continuing through the branch points: ensureChildNodes' EMPTY_NODES check, hasAttributes' null check, accumulateParents' recursive parent condition, childElementsList's shadow reference and instanceof loops, textNodes/dataNodes' typed loops, insertChildren's negative index adjustments, and cssSelector's id/class length checks. I'm now tracking the remaining structural checks: siblingElements and nextElementSibling's null/index boundary conditions, elementSiblingIndex's parent-null shortcut, indexInList's linear search, and getElementsByAttributeValueMatching's regex try/catch for invalid patterns. I'm then examining the text-extraction logic -- the NodeVisitor in text() that decides when to insert whitespace between text nodes and block elements, wholeText's raw text node accumulation, ownText's per-child text gathering, and the start of appendNormalisedText's whitespace-preservation branch. Continuing through appendWhitespaceIfBr for `
` handling, preserveWhitespace which walks up to six ancestor elements checking their tags, the plain text(String) method, hasText's recursive check for non-blank content, and the beginning of data()'s branching logic for extracting script/style content. Now I'm mapping out the class-related methods: className just trims an attribute, classNames splits on whitespace, classNames(Set) branches on whether the resulting set is empty, hasClass checks multiple conditions, and the toggle variants branch on whether the class list already contains the target. I also note val() and val(String) both branch depending on whether the tag is a textarea, and I'm starting to trace outerHtmlHead's pretty-printing logic, which checks accumulator type and indentation before deciding whether child nodes are empty. Given the scale of all these branches, I'm deciding to write a fairly large but manageable test suite covering the most important paths, calling out in comments where some of the deeply nested formatting logic is too intricate to fully exercise. I'm planning around 70-90 test methods organized with helper methods for building elements and tags, and I need to confirm that Tag.valueOf works as expected and that common tags like div and p are treated as block elements while span is inline. I'm also checking that br is self-closing, pre and textarea preserve whitespace, and that the Document class extends Element with its root tag likely named "#root". Document.OutputSettings is a standard nested static class with prettyPrint, outline, and syntax methods, plus an html/xml Syntax enum -- I need to make sure I'm matching this exact API given how risky mismatches could be here. I'm leaning toward writing the test class now with reasonable coverage, flagging areas where I'm uncertain about internal API details like NodeUtils or Tag specifics with comments rather than guessing wildly, and possibly minimizing reliance on the output formatting methods since their exact signatures aren't fully confirmed. Since jsoup is a well-known codebase, I'm confident the standard public methods like outerHtml() exist on Node and can be used to indirectly exercise outerHtmlHead/outerHtmlTail logic without calling those package-private methods directly, so I'll test through that public API with varying OutputSettings configurations. I should follow the instruction not to guess behavior absent from the given source, so I'll comment on that assumption and limit testing to what's actually defined: the package-private methods ensureChildNodes, hasAttributes, nodelistChanged, doSetBaseUri, and outerHtmlHead/outerHtmlTail, which I can call directly since they're in the same package. For outerHtmlHead/outerHtmlTail, I'll construct a minimal Document and OutputSettings instance, noting that I'm assuming standard jsoup API behavior for those since they aren't shown directly. Given the scope here, I'll focus my effort on solid tests for the core Element logic that's explicitly provided. I'll assume DataNode, Comment, and CDataNode all have simple public constructors taking a string, consistent with recent jsoup versions, flagging any uncertainty in comments. For the hasClass tests, I'm crafting cases like "one two three" matched against "two", "tw", and "our" to exercise substring edge cases, plus checking the end-of-string branch in the matching loop. Since no whitespace is hit, inClass stays true until the loop ends, so the final check catches it: length 7-2=5 matches wantLen, and "alpha" correctly matches "alpha". I should also verify a case with multiple classes like "alpha beta gamma" searching for "beta" to confirm the whitespace-triggered comparison works mid-string, and test a mismatched length case like "bet" against "beta" to ensure it correctly rejects due to length difference. Now I need to test invalid regex handling for getElementsByAttributeValueMatching and similar methods, confirming a PatternSyntaxException gets wrapped as IllegalArgumentException. I also want to check insertChildren's boundary behavior—negative index wrapping to the end, out-of-range negative indices throwing via Validate.isTrue, and null children triggering Validate.notNull—plus verify child(int index) properly throws when out of bounds. I'm also tracing through cssSelector generation for a nested span inside a div with sibling spans, walking through how the selector string gets built up with nth-child logic and parent traversal. Tracing further, parent.cssSelector() for div with no id, no class, and no parent returns just "div", so the final result becomes "div > span:nth-child(2)" which matches expected jsoup output—I'll assert that exact string. I also want to test the id case separately, since cssSelector() should immediately return "#foo" when an id is present, bypassing class and parent logic, and then test the no-parent/no-id case with a class attribute. For multi-class selectors, I'm checking that classNames() preserves insertion order via a LinkedHashSet, so "header gray" joins to "header.gray" and the selector becomes "div.header.gray". I'll also verify the simplest case—no classes, no id, no parent—just returns the tag name alone, then move on to testing siblingElements() to confirm it excludes the element itself while including its other siblings. Next I need to check nextElementSibling and previousElementSibling edge cases: last child's next should be null, first child's previous should be null, and the middle cases should return the correct adjacent element. I'm also looking at firstElementSibling and lastElementSibling, where the implementation only returns a boundary element when there's more than one sibling in the parent's list—otherwise it returns null even though the single element is technically both first and last. The "not found" branch of indexInList isn't easily testable through the public API since parent-child relationships are managed internally, so I'll skip that edge case. Now I'm planning the data() test combining DataNode, Comment, nested Element with DataNode, and CDataNode children, then composing the final test file with the right package and imports, including Tag.valueOf for creating standard elements like div, span, and p. I want around 60 test methods covering block vs inline behavior for tags like div, span, br, pre, textarea, a, b, script, and style, so I'll verify isBlock() returns true for div and false for span as a sanity check, then write the full code with a compact summary table grouping similar tests together to keep things manageable given the large scope. I'm confirming that jsoup's Validate.notNull and Validate.notEmpty both throw IllegalArgumentException when given invalid input, which I'll need to account for in the exception-handling tests. Now writing JUnit test cases... I should also verify that NodeList invalidates its cached children correctly—calling children() to build the cache, appending a new child, then calling children() again should reflect the update since the cache gets cleared through the nodelistChanged callback. I also want to test clone() behavior: cloning an element with children should preserve the structure (tag name, child count) while keeping the lists independent, so mutating the original afterward doesn't affect the clone. Similarly, shallowClone() should copy the tag, baseUri, and attributes but produce zero children regardless of the original's child count, and I should check that attr("disabled", true) properly sets the boolean attribute so it can be retrieved via attributes().getIgnoreCase(). To avoid risk I'll just stick with default OutputSettings rather than toggling prettyPrint, assuming the default pretty-print behavior covers one branch; I'll note the assumption about the fluent setter but not rely on it further given time constraints. I don't need to know the exact original defect for this Defects4J case—thorough tests should suffice. Now I'm writing the actual test class with minimal setup, moving straight to the implementation. I'm verifying the jsoup API I'll be targeting, around version 1.11-1.12, confirming that DataNode and Comment both have simple single-argument constructors extending LeafNode. Checking CDataNode and TextNode constructors, Document's baseUri constructor, and Tag.valueOf's signature to confirm the API details line up for the Element construction path. These methods are confirmed accessible since Element's source already calls them directly. Now I'll draft the final test file, aiming for roughly 550-700 lines, making sure methods like outerHtmlHead/Tail declare IOException, and verifying Elements has nextAll/prevAll, QueryParser.parse is public static, and that Evaluator.Tag is a usable public inner class for the is(Evaluator) test. I'm ready to write out the complete test class now.
